```{r configuration}
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 0. WHY THIS SCRIPT EXISTS
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 02_Reduction_Stage.Rmd pools all 80 raw need items into one flat mixed-
# type correlation matrix and gets KMO = 0.153 (unacceptable, Kaiser 1974).
# 02c_Reduction_Stage_WS1Needs.Rmd pools only the 45 WS1-documented items
# (C5c/F9a/F10/F5, dropping F1/F3/buying-criteria/category-perception) and
# gets KMO = 0.973 (marvelous). Diagnosis (established in chat, not
# re-derived here): C5c/F9a/F10 individually scored KMO 0.90-0.96 in
# Workstream 1's own block-level EFA, and the 45-item pool's strong overall
# KMO shows C5c+F9a+F10+F5 already share enough cross-block variance to
# pool directly. F1 and F3 (30 items, current/planned tech adoption +
# future-usefulness endorsement for the same technology list) are the
# blocks that do NOT share that variance -- adding them to a flat pooled
# matrix doesn't just fail to help, it drags every other item's MSA down
# too, because KMO's partial correlation controls for every other item at
# once (see reduction_item_msa.png from the 80-item run: literally all 80
# items fail the 0.6 floor, including C5c items that scored 0.90+ alone).
#
# THIS SCRIPT keeps every one of the 80 items in play, but stops asking one
# flat correlation matrix to explain all of them at once:
#   STAGE 1: F1, F3, and a 5-item "ProviderPerception" block each get their
#     own within-block suitability check + EFA (mirroring how Workstream 1
#     already did this successfully for C5c/F9a/F10 individually) --
#     varimax/orthogonal rotation, since a single narrow battery is exactly
#     the case where near-independent factors are plausible a priori (same
#     justification WS1 used). C5c/F9a/F10/F5's OWN-NEED items (the 45-item
#     pool minus the 5 ProviderPerception items below) are NOT re-done here
#     -- 02c already reduced them cleanly (KMO=0.973, 5 reliable factors)
#     and that result is reused directly, not re-computed.
#
#     ProviderPerception is a NEW block added here (not present in the
#     75-item version of this script) to close the gap identified when
#     verifying "are all 80 items used": C5c_2r6 ("Providers understand the
#     needs of modern businesses") and F10r2/r3/r7/r15 ("A well-known
#     provider" / "Easy to access stores" / "Cheap prices" / "A company we
#     can trust") were excluded from 02c's 45-item WS1-documented pool
#     because WS1's own D1/D3 documents scoped them as provider-selection/
#     buying-criteria items, not own-company operational needs -- a
#     legitimate conceptual distinction, but one that meant they were never
#     actually reduced or scored anywhere in this pipeline family. Grouping
#     them into their own block lets the data test whether they cohere as a
#     "how we judge/perceive a provider" dimension, on the same footing as
#     every other block, rather than either silently dropping them or
#     forcing them into blocks they don't conceptually belong to.
#   STAGE 2: the resulting block-level factor scores (5 from 02c + however
#     many F1 produces + however many F3 produces + however many
#     ProviderPerception produces) are combined into one respondent-level,
#     ALL-CONTINUOUS dataset. A second KMO/Bartlett check on THIS combined
#     set is the headline diagnostic this script exists to produce -- if the
#     hierarchical restructuring worked, this should sit far above 0.153
#     (though, being a much smaller and already-reduced set of continuous
#     scores rather than 80 raw mixed-type items, it is not numerically
#     comparable to either prior KMO on a like-for-like basis; it answers
#     "do these block-level summaries cohere", not "do the raw items
#     cohere").
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------
ws1_reduction_rds <- "workstream2c_outputs_ws1needs/reduction_stage_objects_ws1needs.rds"
data_path      <- "client_survey_data.xlsx"  # NOT INCLUDED in this repository -- see ../../../data/README.md
value_map_path <- "value_label_map.csv"  # NOT INCLUDED -- original survey instrument wording is confidential
output_dir        <- "workstream2d_outputs_hierarchical"
dir.create(output_dir, showWarnings = FALSE)

set.seed(1526)

LOADING_CUTOFF   <- 0.40   # Albert (2003) / Dibb & Wensley (2002), consistent with the other scripts
ALPHA_MIN        <- 0.70   # Nunnally (1978)
KMO_MIN          <- 0.60   # Kaiser (1974) floor
FACTOR_MIN_BLOCK <- 1      # sub-blocks are single narrow batteries -- unlike the pooled
                           # stages (FACTOR_MIN=4), a clean 1-factor (summated-scale)
                           # outcome is a perfectly good, arguably more interpretable,
                           # result here, not a sign the search under-shot.
```

```{r load-ws1-factors}
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. LOAD STAGE 1 (ALREADY DONE): THE 45-ITEM POOL'S 5 RELIABLE FA FACTORS
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------
stopifnot(
  "02c_Reduction_Stage_WS1Needs.Rmd output not found -- knit that script first" =
    file.exists(ws1_reduction_rds)
)
ws1_obj <- readRDS(ws1_reduction_rds)
stopifnot(
  "reduction_stage_objects_ws1needs.rds is missing expected components -- re-knit 02c_Reduction_Stage_WS1Needs.Rmd" =
    all(c("fa_scores", "uuid", "firmographics", "factor_reliability") %in% names(ws1_obj))
)

need_fa_scores <- as.data.frame(ws1_obj$fa_scores)
colnames(need_fa_scores) <- paste0("NeedFA", seq_len(ncol(need_fa_scores)))
cat("Loaded", ncol(need_fa_scores), "reliable FA factor(s) from the 45-item WS1 pool for",
    nrow(need_fa_scores), "respondents.\n")
print(ws1_obj$factor_reliability[, c("factor", "n_items", "cronbach_alpha", "reliable")])

need_fa_df <- bind_cols(tibble(uuid = ws1_obj$uuid), as_tibble(need_fa_scores))
```

block_ProviderPerception <- c(

block_F3 <- c(

  F3r4  = "Satellite / Non-Terrestrial Network connectivity",

  F3r15 = "Next-gen predictive cybersecurity"
)

block_F1 <- setNames(unname(block_F3),
                      c("F1r1","F1r2","F1r3","F1r4","F1r5","F1r6","F1r7","F1r8",

```{r recoding}
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 3.1 RECODING (identical logic/rationale to 02_Reduction_Stage.Rmd)
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------
recode_from_map <- function(data, vars, value_map) {
  for (v in vars) {
    lookup  <- value_map %>% filter(variable == v) %>% select(label, code) %>% distinct()
    map_vec <- setNames(lookup$code, lookup$label)
    data[[v]] <- unname(map_vec[as.character(data[[v]])])
  }
  data
}
recode_checkbox <- function(x) {
  ifelse(is.na(x), NA_real_,
         ifelse(stringr::str_starts(trimws(as.character(x)), "NO TO:"), 0, 1))
}
rebase_need_intensity <- function(x) {
  ifelse(x %in% 1:5, 6 - x, NA_real_)   # code 6 ("not relevant") -> NA
}
extract_leading_int <- function(x) {
  as.numeric(stringr::str_extract(trimws(as.character(x)), "^\\d+"))
}

# F1: exact-label recode, then re-based to a 1-5 need-intensity scale
# (5 = currently use, 1 = not interested) -- same treatment as F5 elsewhere.
df <- recode_from_map(df, names(block_F1), value_map)
df[names(block_F1)] <- lapply(df[names(block_F1)], rebase_need_intensity)

# F3: binary checkbox recode ("NO TO: ..." prefix = not endorsed).
df[names(block_F3)] <- lapply(df[names(block_F3)], recode_checkbox)

# ROBUSTNESS (added on code review): recode_checkbox matches a literal
# "NO TO:" string prefix -- any label drift (typo, re-wording) would
# silently fall through to "endorsed" (1) rather than raising an error.
# F3 later returns a genuinely degenerate KMO (~0.02); before treating that
# as a substantive finding rather than a recoding artefact, print each
# item's endorsement rate so a rival explanation ("everything coded 1
# because the string match failed") is checked, not assumed away (Browne's
# Ten Critical Questions: are there rival explanations for this statistic?).
f3_endorsement_rates <- sapply(df[names(block_F3)], function(x) mean(x == 1, na.rm = TRUE))
cat("F3 item endorsement rates (share coded 1, i.e. NOT 'NO TO:'):\n")
print(round(sort(f3_endorsement_rates), 3))
if (any(f3_endorsement_rates > 0.98) || any(f3_endorsement_rates < 0.02)) {
  cat("WARNING: at least one F3 item has a near-constant endorsement rate (>98% or <2%) --",
      "check this item's raw label text/value_map entry before trusting F3's KMO as a genuine",
      "finding rather than a recoding artefact.\n")
}

# ProviderPerception: C5c_2r6 -- REVERSE-CODED, same fix and same reasoning
# as block_C5c in 02c_Reduction_Stage_WS1Needs.Rmd (2026-08): C5c's raw 1-7
# codes run opposite to every other scale in this survey (confirmed via
# cross-check against F5, not from documented scale anchors -- see 02c
# Section 3.2 for the full evidence). F10r2/r3/r7/r15 are the hybrid
# numeric/label 1-7 scale used for the rest of F10 (extract_leading_int) --
# F10 IS documented low->high importance in the questionnaire, so those are
# unaffected and need no re-basing.
df[["C5c_2r6"]] <- 8 - as.numeric(df[["C5c_2r6"]])
df[c("F10r2", "F10r3", "F10r7", "F10r15")] <-
  lapply(df[c("F10r2", "F10r3", "F10r7", "F10r15")], extract_leading_int)

f1_raw <- as.data.frame(df[, names(block_F1)])
f3_raw <- as.data.frame(df[, names(block_F3)])
provider_perception_raw <- as.data.frame(df[, names(block_ProviderPerception)])

cat("F1 block:", nrow(f1_raw), "respondents x", ncol(f1_raw), "items | missingness range:",
    round(min(sapply(f1_raw, function(x) mean(is.na(x)))) * 100, 1), "% -",
    round(max(sapply(f1_raw, function(x) mean(is.na(x)))) * 100, 1), "%\n")
cat("F3 block:", nrow(f3_raw), "respondents x", ncol(f3_raw), "items | missingness range:",
    round(min(sapply(f3_raw, function(x) mean(is.na(x)))) * 100, 1), "% -",
    round(max(sapply(f3_raw, function(x) mean(is.na(x)))) * 100, 1), "%\n")
cat("ProviderPerception block:", nrow(provider_perception_raw), "respondents x",
    ncol(provider_perception_raw), "items | missingness range:",
    round(min(sapply(provider_perception_raw, function(x) mean(is.na(x)))) * 100, 1), "% -",
    round(max(sapply(provider_perception_raw, function(x) mean(is.na(x)))) * 100, 1), "%\n")
```

```{r block-efa-function}
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 4. REUSABLE WITHIN-BLOCK REDUCTION FUNCTION
#    Same interpretability-screened factor-count search used pipeline-wide
#    (02_Reduction_Stage.Rmd / 02c's Section 8), generalised into one
#    function so it can be applied to F1 and F3 without duplicating ~150
#    lines of logic twice. VARIMAX (orthogonal), not oblimin: a single
#    narrow battery about one topic is exactly the case Workstream 1 used
#    varimax for -- near-independent factors are plausible a priori within
#    one block, unlike the pooled multi-block stages (02/02c), where
#    oblique rotation was justified because correlated need dimensions
#    become plausible once distinct blocks are combined (Costello &
#    Osborne, 2005).
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------
alpha_reverse_scored <- function(raw_data, member_vars, loading_signs) {
  item_data <- raw_data[, member_vars, drop = FALSE]
  flip <- member_vars[loading_signs < 0]
  if (length(flip) > 0) item_data[flip] <- -1 * item_data[flip]
  suppressWarnings(psych::alpha(item_data, check.keys = FALSE))
}

run_block_reduction <- function(raw_data, item_labels, block_name, cor_type,
                                 factor_min = FACTOR_MIN_BLOCK,
                                 loading_cutoff = LOADING_CUTOFF,
                                 alpha_min = ALPHA_MIN) {

  cat("\n==============================\nBLOCK:", block_name, "\n")
  vars <- names(item_labels)
  n_avail <- colSums(!is.na(raw_data[vars]))
  n_obs   <- round(mean(n_avail))

  # --- ROBUSTNESS 1: per-item missingness table (not just the block-level
  # min/max range printed at import time) -- an auditable record of exactly
  # how much each item was imputed before scoring, and the trigger for the
  # complete-case sensitivity check below. ---------------------------------
  item_missingness <- tibble(block = block_name, variable = vars,
                              item_label = unname(item_labels[vars]),
                              pct_missing = round((1 - n_avail / nrow(raw_data)) * 100, 1))
  cat(block_name, "item missingness (%):\n")
  print(item_missingness[order(-item_missingness$pct_missing), c("variable", "pct_missing")])

  # --- correlation matrix: appropriate to this block's single item type ---
  # "pearson" added for ProviderPerception: its 5 items are all 7-point
  # importance scales (>=5 categories), which 02c already treats as
  # continuous for C5c/F9a/F10 under Rhemtulla et al. (2012) -- identical
  # justification, reused rather than re-derived.
  compute_rho <- function(data_subset, method) {
    switch(method,
      "polychoric"  = suppressWarnings(psych::polychoric(data_subset)$rho),
      "tetrachoric" = suppressWarnings(psych::tetrachoric(data_subset)$rho),
      "pearson"     = cor(data_subset, use = "pairwise.complete.obs"),
      stop("cor_type must be 'polychoric', 'tetrachoric', or 'pearson'")
    )
  }
  rho <- compute_rho(raw_data[vars], cor_type)
  dimnames(rho) <- list(vars, vars)

  eig_vals <- eigen(rho, symmetric = TRUE, only.values = TRUE)$values
  n_neg <- sum(eig_vals < -1e-8)
  if (n_neg > 0) {
    cat("WARNING:", block_name, "correlation matrix not positive semi-definite --",
        "applying psych::cor.smooth().\n")
    rho <- psych::cor.smooth(rho)
    dimnames(rho) <- list(vars, vars)
  }

  # --- ROBUSTNESS 2: matrix-conditioning check. Eigenvalue-negativity above
  # only catches non-PD matrices; a matrix can be PD yet numerically
  # ill-conditioned (near-singular), which is exactly the regime the
  # MASS::ginv() scoring step below is compensating for. The condition
  # number (Belsley, Kuh & Welsch, 1980) makes that risk visible rather than
  # silently absorbed by ginv().
  condition_number <- tryCatch(kappa(rho, exact = TRUE), error = function(e) NA_real_)
  cat(block_name, "correlation matrix condition number (exact):", round(condition_number, 1), "\n")
  if (!is.na(condition_number) && condition_number > 1000) {
    cat("WARNING:", block_name, "rho is poorly conditioned (kappa >1000) -- MASS::ginv()",
        "scoring below is the numerically appropriate response, but treat factor scores",
        "from this block as approximate, not exact, regression estimates.\n")
  }

  # --- ROBUSTNESS 3: complete-case sensitivity check, auto-triggered when
  # any item exceeds 20% missingness. Rules out "pairwise-complete-obs
  # correlation estimation is distorting this block's suitability" as a
  # rival explanation (Browne's Ten Critical Questions) before any KMO
  # result below is interpreted substantively.
  complete_case_kmo <- NA_real_
  n_complete_case   <- NA_integer_
  if (max(item_missingness$pct_missing) > 20) {
    cc_idx <- stats::complete.cases(raw_data[vars])
    n_complete_case <- sum(cc_idx)
    cat(block_name, "has an item with >20% missingness -- running a complete-case-only",
        "sensitivity check (n =", n_complete_case, "of", nrow(raw_data), "respondents):\n")
    cc_rho <- tryCatch(compute_rho(raw_data[vars][cc_idx, , drop = FALSE], cor_type),
                        error = function(e) NULL)
    if (!is.null(cc_rho) && !anyNA(cc_rho)) {
      dimnames(cc_rho) <- list(vars, vars)
      complete_case_kmo <- tryCatch(psych::KMO(cc_rho)$MSA, error = function(e) NA_real_)
    }
    if (is.na(complete_case_kmo)) {
      cat("Complete-case correlation/KMO could not be computed (too few complete cases",
          "or a degenerate category) -- skipping this comparison.\n")
    } else {
      cat("Complete-case-only KMO will be compared to the pairwise-complete-obs KMO",
          "once it is computed below.\n")
    }
  }

  kmo_res  <- psych::KMO(rho)
  bart_res <- psych::cortest.bartlett(rho, n = n_obs)
  cat("KMO =", round(kmo_res$MSA, 3), "| Bartlett chi-sq =", round(bart_res$chisq, 1),
      ", df =", bart_res$df, ", p =", signif(bart_res$p.value, 3), "\n")
  if (is.na(kmo_res$MSA) || kmo_res$MSA < KMO_MIN) {
    cat("WARNING: block KMO below", KMO_MIN, "-- inspect before trusting this block's factors.\n")
  }
  if (!is.na(complete_case_kmo)) {
    cat("Complete-case-only KMO =", round(complete_case_kmo, 3),
        "vs pairwise-complete-obs KMO =", round(kmo_res$MSA, 3), "-- ")
    if (abs(complete_case_kmo - kmo_res$MSA) > 0.05) {
      cat("these diverge by more than 0.05: missing-data handling materially affects this",
          "block's suitability estimate, and should be named as a limitation.\n")
    } else {
      cat("these agree closely: the pairwise-complete-obs KMO is not an artefact of how",
          "missing data were handled.\n")
    }
  }

  pa <- psych::fa.parallel(rho, n.obs = n_obs, fa = "fa", n.iter = 100, plot = FALSE)
  n_fact_ceiling <- max(1, pa$nfact)
  cat("Parallel analysis suggests", n_fact_ceiling, "factor(s)\n")

  evaluate_k <- function(k) {
    fit <- tryCatch(
      suppressWarnings(psych::fa(rho, nfactors = k, n.obs = n_obs,
                                  rotate = if (k == 1) "none" else "varimax", fm = "minres")),
      error = function(e) NULL
    )
    if (is.null(fit)) return(NULL)
    heywood <- any(fit$communality > 1.001, na.rm = TRUE)
    load_df <- as.data.frame(unclass(fit$loadings))
    k_cols  <- names(load_df)
    load_df$variable <- rownames(load_df)
    assign_k <- function(row) {
      vals <- as.numeric(row[k_cols])
      best <- which.max(abs(vals))
      if (abs(vals[best]) >= loading_cutoff) k_cols[best] else NA_character_
    }
    load_df$assigned <- apply(load_df[k_cols], 1, assign_k)
    rel <- purrr::map_dfr(k_cols, function(fc) {
      member_vars <- load_df$variable[load_df$assigned == fc & !is.na(load_df$assigned)]
      if (length(member_vars) < 3) {
        return(tibble(factor = fc, n_items = length(member_vars),
                       cronbach_alpha = NA_real_, reliable = FALSE))
      }
      signs <- sign(load_df[[fc]][load_df$variable %in% member_vars])
      a <- alpha_reverse_scored(raw_data, member_vars, signs)
      tibble(factor = fc, n_items = length(member_vars),
             cronbach_alpha = a$total$raw_alpha,
             reliable = isTRUE(a$total$raw_alpha >= alpha_min))
    })
    list(k = k, fit = fit, heywood = heywood,
         n_degenerate = sum(!rel$reliable) + as.integer(heywood),
         n_unassigned = sum(is.na(load_df$assigned)))
  }

  k_candidates <- factor_min:n_fact_ceiling
  search <- purrr::compact(purrr::map(k_candidates, evaluate_k))
  names(search) <- vapply(search, function(r) as.character(r$k), character(1))
  search_summary <- purrr::map_dfr(search, function(r) {
    tibble(k = r$k, heywood_case = r$heywood, n_degenerate_factors = r$n_degenerate,
           n_unassigned_items = r$n_unassigned)
  })
  cat("Factor-count search (k =", factor_min, "to", n_fact_ceiling, "):\n")
  print(search_summary)

  clean_k <- search_summary$k[search_summary$n_degenerate_factors == 0]
  n_fact_optimal <- if (length(clean_k) > 0) max(clean_k) else {
    min_degen <- min(search_summary$n_degenerate_factors)
    kk <- max(search_summary$k[search_summary$n_degenerate_factors == min_degen])
    cat("WARNING: no k fully clean; using k =", kk, "(fewest degenerate factors).\n")
    kk
  }
  cat("Selected", n_fact_optimal, "factor(s) for", block_name, "\n")

  fit <- search[[as.character(n_fact_optimal)]]$fit
  print(fit$loadings, cutoff = loading_cutoff, sort = TRUE)

  loadings_df <- as.data.frame(unclass(fit$loadings)) %>%
    tibble::rownames_to_column("variable") %>%
    mutate(item_label = unname(item_labels[variable]))
  fac_cols <- setdiff(names(loadings_df), c("variable", "item_label"))
  assign_factor <- function(row) {
    vals <- as.numeric(row[fac_cols])
    best <- which.max(abs(vals))
    if (abs(vals[best]) >= loading_cutoff) fac_cols[best] else NA_character_
  }
  loadings_df$assigned_factor <- apply(loadings_df[fac_cols], 1, assign_factor)

  # BUGFIX (2026-08-06, code-review item #1): evaluate_k() above requires
  # >=3 assigned items for a factor to count as non-degenerate during the
  # k-search (fewer items forces reliable=FALSE there, which drives which k
  # gets selected) -- but this final table previously only excluded <2-item
  # factors, so a 2-item factor already treated as "degenerate" during model
  # selection could still be computed a REAL alpha here and reported
  # reliable=TRUE if that alpha happened to clear alpha_min, contradicting
  # its own degeneracy classification from the search. Fixed by capping
  # `reliable` at the same n_items>=3 floor regardless of the computed
  # alpha value -- a 2-item factor can now never show reliable=TRUE here.
  # The numeric alpha itself is still computed and shown for n_items==2
  # (rather than blanked to NA): it remains a useful diagnostic even when
  # not trusted -- e.g. F3_Factor1's alpha=0.263 is itself informative
  # evidence of how weak that 2-item factor is, and hiding it would lose
  # that signal for no real gain. Only n_items<2 (alpha not even computable)
  # returns NA, as before.
  reliability_df <- purrr::map_dfr(fac_cols, function(fc) {
    member_vars <- loadings_df$variable[loadings_df$assigned_factor == fc & !is.na(loadings_df$assigned_factor)]
    if (length(member_vars) < 2) {
      return(tibble(factor = fc, n_items = length(member_vars),
                     items = paste(unname(item_labels[member_vars]), collapse = "; "),
                     cronbach_alpha = NA_real_, reliable = FALSE))
    }
    signs <- sign(loadings_df[[fc]][loadings_df$variable %in% member_vars])
    a <- alpha_reverse_scored(raw_data, member_vars, signs)
    tibble(factor = fc, n_items = length(member_vars),
           items = paste(unname(item_labels[member_vars]), collapse = "; "),
           cronbach_alpha = round(a$total$raw_alpha, 3),
           reliable = (length(member_vars) >= 3) && isTRUE(a$total$raw_alpha >= alpha_min))
  })
  cat("\n", block_name, "factor reliability:\n")
  print(reliability_df)

  # --- respondent-level factor scores ---------------------------------
  # Orthogonal (varimax) rotation when k>1: pattern == structure, so no Phi
  # correction is needed (unlike the pooled oblimin stages). k==1 has no
  # rotation at all ("none" above) -- scoring collapses to the same
  # regression-scoring formula with a single-column loadings matrix.
  raw_imputed <- as.data.frame(lapply(raw_data[vars], function(x) {
    x[is.na(x)] <- stats::median(x, na.rm = TRUE); x
  }))
  z <- scale(as.matrix(raw_imputed))
  weights <- MASS::ginv(rho) %*% unclass(fit$loadings)
  scores <- z %*% weights
  colnames(scores) <- paste0(block_name, "_Factor", seq_len(ncol(scores)))

  score_range <- range(scores)
  cat(block_name, "score range:", round(score_range[1], 2), "to", round(score_range[2], 2), "\n")
  if (max(abs(score_range)) > 20) {
    cat("WARNING:", block_name, "scores exceed a plausible range -- inspect", block_name, "rho.\n")
  }

  # ROBUSTNESS (added on code review): min-max range alone can hide a small
  # number of extreme respondents inside an otherwise reasonable-looking
  # range (a heavy tail, not a shifted range). This matters specifically
  # for a block whose rho is poorly conditioned (see condition_number
  # above): MASS::ginv() on a near-singular matrix can amplify noise in
  # near-null-space directions, so an unstable score may show up as a few
  # extreme outliers rather than a uniformly implausible range. Report the
  # SD and the count of |z|>3 outliers explicitly so this is visible even
  # when the min-max range looks fine.
  score_z <- scale(scores)
  n_outlier_3sd <- sum(abs(score_z) > 3, na.rm = TRUE)
  cat(block_name, "score SD:", paste(round(apply(scores, 2, sd), 2), collapse = ", "),
      "| respondents with |z|>3 on any", block_name, "factor:", n_outlier_3sd,
      "of", nrow(scores), "\n")
  if (!is.na(condition_number) && condition_number > 1e6 && n_outlier_3sd > 0) {
    cat("WARNING:", block_name, "combines a poorly-conditioned rho with", n_outlier_3sd,
        "outlier score(s) -- treat this block's factor scores as noisy for those respondents",
        "specifically, not just generally approximate.\n")
  }

  list(kmo = kmo_res$MSA, bartlett_p = bart_res$p.value, n_factors = n_fact_optimal,
       loadings = loadings_df, reliability = reliability_df, scores = scores,
       search_summary = search_summary, item_missingness = item_missingness,
       condition_number = condition_number, complete_case_kmo = complete_case_kmo,
       n_complete_case = n_complete_case)
}
```

```{r run-f1-f3}
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 5. STAGE 1b: RUN THE WITHIN-BLOCK REDUCTION FOR F1, F3, AND
#    PROVIDERPERCEPTION
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------
f1_result <- run_block_reduction(f1_raw, block_F1, "F1", cor_type = "polychoric")
f3_result <- run_block_reduction(f3_raw, block_F3, "F3", cor_type = "tetrachoric")
pp_result <- run_block_reduction(provider_perception_raw, block_ProviderPerception,
                                  "ProviderPerception", cor_type = "pearson")
```

```{r combine-stage2}
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 6. STAGE 2: COMBINE THE 45-ITEM POOL'S 5 FA FACTORS WITH F1's, F3's, AND
#    PROVIDERPERCEPTION's BLOCK-LEVEL FACTORS INTO ONE RESPONDENT-LEVEL,
#    ALL-CONTINUOUS DATASET (full 80-item coverage)
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------
f1_scores_df <- bind_cols(tibble(uuid = df$uuid), as_tibble(f1_result$scores))
f3_scores_df <- bind_cols(tibble(uuid = df$uuid), as_tibble(f3_result$scores))
pp_scores_df <- bind_cols(tibble(uuid = df$uuid), as_tibble(pp_result$scores))

combined_scores <- need_fa_df %>%
  left_join(f1_scores_df, by = "uuid") %>%
  left_join(f3_scores_df, by = "uuid") %>%
  left_join(pp_scores_df, by = "uuid")

# ROBUSTNESS (added on code review): a duplicate uuid in any of the four
# score tables would silently fan out one of these left_joins (more rows
# out than in), which the NA check below would NOT catch on its own -- a
# fanned-out row still has no missing cells, just extra duplicated rows.
stopifnot(
  "combined_scores has a different respondent count than need_fa_df -- a left_join above fanned out (likely a duplicate uuid in f1/f3/pp_scores_df); investigate before proceeding" =
    nrow(combined_scores) == nrow(need_fa_df)
)

stopifnot(
  "Combined score matrix has missing cells -- every input score set should be complete for all respondents" =
    sum(is.na(combined_scores)) == 0
)

score_cols <- setdiff(names(combined_scores), "uuid")
cat("Combined hierarchical score set:", nrow(combined_scores), "respondents x",
    length(score_cols), "block-level scores:", paste(score_cols, collapse = ", "), "\n")

# --- Stage 2 suitability check: plain Pearson, since every input here is
# already a continuous derived factor score (no more mixed-type problem to
# solve -- that was already handled within each block in Stage 1). This is
# NOT numerically comparable to the 80-item or 45-item KMOs on a like-for-
# like basis: it is a much smaller matrix of already-reduced summaries, and
# answers a different question ("do these block-level summaries cohere"),
# not "do the 80 raw items cohere".
combined_cor <- cor(combined_scores[, score_cols], use = "pairwise.complete.obs")
combined_kmo  <- psych::KMO(combined_cor)
combined_bart <- psych::cortest.bartlett(combined_cor, n = nrow(combined_scores))

cat("\nStage 2 (combined block-level scores) suitability:\n")
cat("KMO =", round(combined_kmo$MSA, 3), "| Bartlett chi-sq =", round(combined_bart$chisq, 1),
    ", df =", combined_bart$df, ", p =", signif(combined_bart$p.value, 3), "\n")
print(round(sort(combined_kmo$MSAi), 3))

# ROBUSTNESS: same condition-number check applied to every Stage 1 block
# (Section 4), applied here to the Stage 2 combined matrix -- this is the
# matrix any downstream multivariate step (e.g. Mahalanobis-based methods)
# would need to invert, so its conditioning matters just as much as each
# block's own rho did.
combined_condition_number <- tryCatch(kappa(combined_cor, exact = TRUE), error = function(e) NA_real_)
cat("Stage 2 combined-score correlation matrix condition number (exact):",
    round(combined_condition_number, 1), "\n")
if (!is.na(combined_condition_number) && combined_condition_number > 1000) {
  cat("WARNING: Stage 2 combined_cor is poorly conditioned (kappa >1000) -- inspect before",
      "trusting downstream multivariate steps that invert it.\n")
}

tryCatch({
  cor_df <- as.data.frame(combined_cor) %>% tibble::rownames_to_column("var1") %>%
    tidyr::pivot_longer(-var1, names_to = "var2", values_to = "rho") %>%
    mutate(var1 = factor(var1, levels = score_cols), var2 = factor(var2, levels = rev(score_cols)))
  p_combined_cor <- ggplot2::ggplot(cor_df, ggplot2::aes(var1, var2, fill = rho)) +
    ggplot2::geom_tile() + ggplot2::geom_text(ggplot2::aes(label = round(rho, 2)), size = 3) +
    ggplot2::scale_fill_gradient2(low = "#B2182B", mid = "white", high = "#2166AC",
                                   midpoint = 0, limits = c(-1, 1), name = "r") +
    ggplot2::labs(title = "Stage 2: correlations among combined block-level scores",
                  subtitle = paste0("Overall KMO = ", round(combined_kmo$MSA, 3)), x = NULL, y = NULL) +
    ggplot2::theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
    ggplot2::theme(axis.text.x = ggplot2::element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))
  print(p_combined_cor)
  ggplot2::ggsave(file.path(output_dir, "hierarchical_stage2_correlation_heatmap.png"),
                   plot = p_combined_cor, width = 8, height = 7, dpi = 300)
}, error = function(e) cat("Stage 2 correlation heatmap skipped:", conditionMessage(e), "\n"))

# NOTE: no further EFA/PCA collapse is forced here. The combined score set
# (5 need factors + F1's + F3's block factors) is already a small number of
# well-behaved continuous variables -- exactly the kind of input Ward's/
# K-means/GMM already expect -- so it is carried into clustering AS-IS.
# Forcing one more reduction pass on top risks re-introducing, in
# miniature, the same pooling problem this whole design exists to avoid.
```

```{r score-traceability}
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 6b. SCORE-TO-RAW-ITEM TRACEABILITY MAP + PER-SCORE RELIABILITY SUMMARY
#     Built so the Clustering Stage can report which raw survey items sit
#     behind each of the combined scores -- WBS Workstream 2 brief asks for
#     "clear rules" and the variables that "define each segment", which is
#     not answerable for this hierarchical design without reconciling FOUR
#     separate loadings matrices (02c's 45-item pool + F1 + F3 +
#     ProviderPerception) into one lookup. Also carries each score's Stage
#     1 reliability verdict forward explicitly, so a score that failed the
#     ALPHA_MIN bar (F3_Factor1, ProviderPerception_Factor1 in the current
#     run) can never be presented downstream as equally trustworthy as one
#     that passed it, without an explicit flag attached.
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 45-item pool's NeedFA1..NeedFAk: column j of ws1_obj$fa_res$loadings is
# NeedFA{j} by construction (see Section 1 -- need_fa_scores/need_fa_df
# already assume this same positional correspondence). factor_reliability
# is matched by NAME (not position) via match(), exactly the same safe
# pattern already used for this same lookup in 02d_Clustering_Hierarchical.Rmd.
ws1_fa_loadings_mat <- unclass(ws1_obj$fa_res$loadings)
ws1_rel_idx <- match(colnames(ws1_fa_loadings_mat), ws1_obj$factor_reliability$factor)

needfa_map <- purrr::map_dfr(seq_len(ncol(ws1_fa_loadings_mat)), function(j) {
  score_col  <- paste0("NeedFA", j)
  loadings_j <- ws1_fa_loadings_mat[, j]
  assigned_vars <- names(loadings_j)[abs(loadings_j) >= LOADING_CUTOFF]
  if (length(assigned_vars) == 0) return(NULL)
  tibble(
    score_col      = score_col,
    source_block   = "45-item WS1 pool (02c)",
    variable       = assigned_vars,
    item_label     = unname(ws1_obj$item_labels[assigned_vars]),
    loading        = round(loadings_j[assigned_vars], 3),
    n_items        = ws1_obj$factor_reliability$n_items[ws1_rel_idx[j]],
    cronbach_alpha = ws1_obj$factor_reliability$cronbach_alpha[ws1_rel_idx[j]],
    reliable       = ws1_obj$factor_reliability$reliable[ws1_rel_idx[j]]
  )
})

# F1/F3/ProviderPerception: score column names are "{block_name}_Factor{i}"
# where i indexes fac_cols in the SAME order run_block_reduction() used to
# build `scores` (see Section 4's "colnames(scores) <- paste0(block_name,
# '_Factor', seq_len(ncol(scores)))") -- reproduced here by position, not
# assumed to always be a single factor, so this stays correct even if a
# future re-knit selects k>1 for one of these blocks.
block_result_map <- function(result, score_prefix, source_block) {
  ld <- result$loadings
  fac_cols <- setdiff(names(ld), c("variable", "item_label", "assigned_factor"))
  purrr::map_dfr(seq_along(fac_cols), function(i) {
    fc <- fac_cols[i]
    score_col <- paste0(score_prefix, "_Factor", i)
    rows <- ld[!is.na(ld$assigned_factor) & ld$assigned_factor == fc, ]
    if (nrow(rows) == 0) return(NULL)
    rel_row <- result$reliability[result$reliability$factor == fc, ]
    tibble(
      score_col      = score_col,
      source_block   = source_block,
      variable       = rows$variable,
      item_label     = rows$item_label,
      loading        = round(rows[[fc]], 3),
      n_items        = if (nrow(rel_row) > 0) rel_row$n_items[1] else nrow(rows),
      cronbach_alpha = if (nrow(rel_row) > 0) rel_row$cronbach_alpha[1] else NA_real_,
      reliable       = if (nrow(rel_row) > 0) rel_row$reliable[1] else NA
    )
  })
}

score_item_map <- bind_rows(
  needfa_map,
  block_result_map(f1_result, "F1", "F1 block (within-block EFA, 02d)"),
  block_result_map(f3_result, "F3", "F3 block (within-block EFA, 02d)"),
  block_result_map(pp_result, "ProviderPerception", "ProviderPerception block (within-block EFA, 02d)")
)

# Per-score-column reliability summary -- ONE row per column of
# combined_scores (via a left_join against score_cols, not just the rows
# that happened to have an assigned item), so a hypothetical score with
# zero items above the loading cutoff would still appear here as an
# explicit NA/unreliable row rather than silently vanishing.
score_reliability <- tibble(score_col = score_cols) %>%
  left_join(
    score_item_map %>% distinct(score_col, source_block, n_items, cronbach_alpha, reliable),
    by = "score_col"
  )
cat("\nScore reliability summary (carried forward to the Clustering Stage):\n")
print(score_reliability)

n_unreliable_scores <- sum(score_reliability$reliable %in% FALSE)
if (n_unreliable_scores > 0) {
  cat("\nNOTE:", n_unreliable_scores, "of", nrow(score_reliability),
      "combined scores failed the ALPHA_MIN =", ALPHA_MIN, "reliability bar (",
      paste(score_reliability$score_col[score_reliability$reliable %in% FALSE], collapse = ", "),
      ") -- these are still carried into clustering (dropping them silently would lose real,",
      "if noisily-measured, item coverage), but the Clustering Stage's robustness check re-runs",
      "the recommended solution without them so their influence on segment boundaries is",
      "reported explicitly, not assumed away.\n")
}

# Compact one-row-per-block diagnostics summary (KMO, condition number,
# complete-case sensitivity KMO, retained factor count) for the three
# blocks newly added in this script -- lets a reader see all three
# robustness checks side by side without re-reading the console log.
block_diagnostics <- tibble(
  block             = c("F1", "F3", "ProviderPerception"),
  kmo               = c(f1_result$kmo, f3_result$kmo, pp_result$kmo),
  condition_number  = round(c(f1_result$condition_number, f3_result$condition_number,
                               pp_result$condition_number), 1),
  complete_case_kmo = c(f1_result$complete_case_kmo, f3_result$complete_case_kmo,
                        pp_result$complete_case_kmo),
  n_factors_selected = c(f1_result$n_factors, f3_result$n_factors, pp_result$n_factors)
)
cat("\nBlock diagnostics summary:\n"); print(block_diagnostics)

item_missingness_all <- bind_rows(f1_result$item_missingness, f3_result$item_missingness,
                                   pp_result$item_missingness)
```

```{r save-outputs}
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 7. SAVE OUTPUTS FOR THE CLUSTERING STAGE
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------
writexl::write_xlsx(
  list(
    "Combined Respondent Scores" = combined_scores,
    "F1 Loadings"                = f1_result$loadings,
    "F1 Reliability"             = f1_result$reliability,
    "F1 Factor Search"          = f1_result$search_summary,
    "F3 Loadings"                = f3_result$loadings,
    "F3 Reliability"             = f3_result$reliability,
    "F3 Factor Search"          = f3_result$search_summary,
    "ProviderPerception Loadings"     = pp_result$loadings,
    "ProviderPerception Reliability"  = pp_result$reliability,
    "ProviderPerception Factor Search" = pp_result$search_summary,
    "Stage 2 Suitability"        = tibble(
      metric = c("F1 block KMO", "F1 Bartlett p", "F1 n_factors", "F1 condition number", "F1 complete-case KMO",
                 "F3 block KMO", "F3 Bartlett p", "F3 n_factors", "F3 condition number", "F3 complete-case KMO",
                 "ProviderPerception block KMO", "ProviderPerception Bartlett p", "ProviderPerception n_factors",
                 "ProviderPerception condition number", "ProviderPerception complete-case KMO",
                 "Stage 2 combined KMO", "Stage 2 Bartlett p", "Stage 2 condition number", "N respondents"),
      value  = c(round(f1_result$kmo, 3), signif(f1_result$bartlett_p, 3), f1_result$n_factors,
                 round(f1_result$condition_number, 1), round(f1_result$complete_case_kmo, 3),
                 round(f3_result$kmo, 3), signif(f3_result$bartlett_p, 3), f3_result$n_factors,
                 round(f3_result$condition_number, 1), round(f3_result$complete_case_kmo, 3),
                 round(pp_result$kmo, 3), signif(pp_result$bartlett_p, 3), pp_result$n_factors,
                 round(pp_result$condition_number, 1), round(pp_result$complete_case_kmo, 3),
                 round(combined_kmo$MSA, 3), signif(combined_bart$p.value, 3),
                 round(combined_condition_number, 1), nrow(combined_scores))
    ),
    "Item Missingness"           = item_missingness_all,
    "Block Diagnostics Summary"  = block_diagnostics,
    "Score-to-Item Map"          = score_item_map,
    "Score Reliability Summary"  = score_reliability
  ),
  path = file.path(output_dir, "Workstream2d_Reduction_Stage_Hierarchical.xlsx")
)

saveRDS(list(combined_scores = combined_scores, score_cols = score_cols,
             uuid = df$uuid, firmographics = ws1_obj$firmographics,
             f1_reliability = f1_result$reliability, f3_reliability = f3_result$reliability,
             pp_reliability = pp_result$reliability,
             combined_kmo = combined_kmo$MSA,
             combined_condition_number = combined_condition_number,
             score_item_map = score_item_map, score_reliability = score_reliability,
             block_diagnostics = block_diagnostics, item_missingness = item_missingness_all),
        file.path(output_dir, "hierarchical_reduction_objects.rds"))

cat("\nOutputs written to:", normalizePath(output_dir), "\n")
cat("-> Workstream2d_Reduction_Stage_Hierarchical.xlsx (F1/F3/ProviderPerception block loadings+reliability, combined scores, Stage 2 suitability, item missingness, score traceability + reliability)\n")
cat("-> hierarchical_reduction_objects.rds (combined score set + score-to-item map + reliability flags for the Clustering stage, full 80-item coverage)\n")
```
